title: CloudFront: fast delivery without mixing private users
outcome: Choose cache keys, origin access, and freshness rules for assets and authorized downloads.
useCase: Vue assets and controlled download delivery.
benefits: Lower origin load and faster geographically distributed reads.
drawbacks: Cache identity, invalidation, and asset compatibility add correctness work.
version: AWS SDK for Ruby v3 · service-specific setup · no cloud resources created automatically
cue: A cache key is a sharing decision.

trace.title: Request identity
trace.detail: CloudFront is an edge delivery/cache layer in front of an origin. Static versioned assets are a natural fit. Dynamic or personalized responses require a deliberate cache key and authorization policy.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Browser request → edge key lookup → cached response or origin fetch → response headers → app behavior. Trace a permission change and decide whether an already cached/signed response remains usable.

For deployment, keep the HTML shell and referenced asset versions compatible. A stale shell pointing to removed files can break the app even when the new bundle is correct.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Caching personalized JSON under one shared key is dangerous. Removing old assets immediately can break clients with cached HTML. An invalidation is not a substitute for a correct cache policy.
